long_biography.plain_text:
Boston College preceded Wee Teng Yuan's entry into Kheng Leong in March 2017. He joined as the third generation of his family to work at the Singapore investment and property-development group. His father, Wee Ee Chao, leads the private company, while his grandfather Wee Cho Yaw had earlier transformed it from commodity trading into an investment platform. Wee began in business development and worked on MeyerHouse, a boutique residential project shaped around large-format homes and design longevity.

Today, Wee appears publicly as Kheng Leong's deputy director on new residential launches. This is an active operating role, not merely a family-name association. UOL's latest shareholder materials also attribute to him a deemed interest in 274,103 UOL shares held by Protheus Investment Holdings. The same interest is attributed to three siblings, and the filing records no direct shares in his name. It does not disclose his ownership percentage in Protheus or Kheng Leong. Consequently, the family company's projects, UOL's assets and the broader banking fortune cannot be assigned to Wee personally. Real estate is his current industry; the original mechanism and transfer history of his individual wealth remain Unknown.
